series_short_description: Thrown out at eighteen for refusing to split up, triplets Luke, Tessa, and Sadie build a life in the deep woods.
series_description: All their lives, fraternal brother Luke Bridger and his identical twin sisters Tessa and Sadie wanted to do everything together—and all their lives, their parents screamed at them to spread their wings and go separate ways. Thrown out on their eighteenth birthday for refusing to separate, the three step past the back boundary fence into the vast, non-volcanic Kettle River wilderness of Colville National Forest with three canvas packs, a weathered dome tent, Grandpa Owen's tool roll, and his 1974 acoustic guitar. One blissful first night without shouting turns into a daring pact to stay—forcing you to choose at every Story Crossroads how they gather food, engineer shelter from fallen cedar and living granite, and survive before October snow.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Five Miles Past the Wire
parts.location: Colville National Forest, Kettle River Range, Ferry County, Washington
parts.excerpt: The bottom strand of rusted barbed wire groaned under my boot heel as I held the middle wire up by a weathered tamarack post so Tessa and Sadie could duck through with Grandpa Owen's guitar case. Down through…
parts.image_alt: Eighteen-year-old triplets Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Bridger sitting close together by a warm stone keyhole campfire in front of their blue-and-white dome tent beside a clear mountain stream under twilight Colville National Forest pines, as Sadie fingerpicks Grandpa Owen's vintage spruce-top acoustic guitar.

images.alt: Eighteen-year-old triplets Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Bridger sitting close together by a warm stone keyhole campfire in front of their blue-and-white dome tent beside a clear mountain stream under twilight Colville National Forest pines, as Sadie fingerpicks Grandpa Owen's vintage spruce-top acoustic guitar.

parts.location: Cedar Run Creek, Colville National Forest, Washington
parts.excerpt: Sunlight woke us—not an alarm clock, not knuckles hammering on hollow-core bedroom doors, just warm gold filtering through green pine needles and painting bright dappled coins across the blue nylon tent wall…
parts.image_alt: Folded denim jeans, faded olive flannel, cream henley, navy-striped shirt, and leather work boots stacked neatly dry on a sun-warmed gray granite boulder beside a misty emerald mountain creek pool in Colville National Forest, while Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Bridger laugh collarbone-deep in the brisk snowmelt water.

parts.location: Cedar Run Valley, Colville National Forest, Washington
parts.excerpt: On our second full morning in the woods, Tessa spread a clean cotton bandana flat on the granite hearth-slab and poured out every dry ration left in our three packs so nobody could kid themselves about the math…

crossroads.title: Three Footholds in Cedar Run Valley: Where Do Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Build?
crossroads.prompt: With four days of pantry oats left in their packs and zero intention of walking back out to a town, the triplets have scouted three completely wild footholds inside the Cedar Run basin—each offering its own shelter engineering and wild food supply. All three routes forward are complete, coequal stories.

options.label: The Creek-Bend Cedar Bench
options.subtitle: Stay above the emerald trout pools beside the eighty-foot windfall red cedar—splitting straight cedar planks and roof shakes with Grandpa Owen's froe while weaving willow traps for cutthroat trout.

options.label: The South-Facing Granite Overhang
options.subtitle: Climb half a mile upslope to the bone-dry bedrock cliff alcove overlooking five acres of wild mountain huckleberries and wild onions—walling in the front with flat granite slabs so sun-baked stone radiates warmth all night.

options.label: The Forgotten Stone Springhouse
options.subtitle: Follow the cold spring up to the high tamarack saddle where sixty years of moss hide four intact 1930s fieldstone walls and a 42-degree indoor spring trough—raising new fir rafters beside golden chanterelle and berry woods.

parts.location: The South-Facing Granite Overhang, Cedar Run Slope, Colville National Forest, Washington
parts.excerpt: By eight in the morning, while cool blue shadow still lingered down in the narrow creek bottom, our south-facing granite overhang half a mile upslope was already bathed in warm gold sunlight. We struck the…
parts.image_alt: Beneath a wide, sun-warmed south-facing granite cliff overhang overlooking a lush mountain huckleberry meadow in Colville National Forest, Luke, Tessa, and Sadie Bridger stack flat granite fieldstones and peeled lodgepole pine poles to enclose their rock shelter.

parts.location: The Forgotten Stone Springhouse, High Tamarack Saddle, Colville National Forest, Washington
parts.excerpt: Whoever had laid the four fieldstone walls on the high tamarack saddle back in the nineteen-thirties had built as if they expected the mountain itself to lean on their work. Once Tessa, Sadie, and I cleared out…
parts.image_alt: In a sunlit high mountain tamarack clearing in Colville National Forest, Luke and Tessa Bridger hoist peeled Douglas fir roof rafters onto the moss-covered dry-stone walls of a forgotten 1930s springhouse while Sadie hands up wide strips of western red cedar bark.
